name: com.infrarabbit/data
title: InfraRabbit
description: Published list prices of compute (VPS, GPU hours, LLM tokens, media), archived daily. Read-only.

tools.name: best_price
tools.description: One short answer to 'what does X cost right now?': the best current list price for a model, GPU or VPS plan named in words ('claude opus', 'gpt-5 mini', 'H100', 'hetzner cx22'), from the provider's own page or API first. Returns one `answer` sentence (name, price, unit, read date, source), the one `best` row and at most two `alternatives`, a few hundred bytes in all. Use this first; use search_skus for the full list, cheapest_for_spec to rank by a minimum spec, get_price for every price point of one SKU. Returns an error object when nothing matches, with near matches.

query.description: What to price, in words: 'claude opus', 'h100', 'llama 3.3 70b', 'ovhcloud vps-1'
query.title: Query

category.description: vps, gpu or llm; omit to search all
category.title: Category

tools.name: search_skus
tools.description: Find VPS plans, GPU instances or LLM models by words ('openai gpt-5', 'H200', 'official anthropic', 'gemini 3'): every word must be in the SKU id or name; 'official' and lab names are signals. Rows come first-party first (the provider's own price, source_class first_party), then resellers (Amazon Bedrock, Azure ...), then community catalogues (models.dev, LiteLLM, OpenRouter), each row labelled with source_class. gpu and vps rows follow `commitment` (default on-demand: spot and committed prices are left out, as in cheapest_for_spec). Answers with a short `answer` sentence first (human names, price, VAT basis, term, read date, source), then compact rows; verbose=true returns every field of every row. No hit: near matches and did_you_mean. Active SKUs on the provider's public price page or product API by default (listing filter). Read-only; reads the ledger's own daily archive, nothing is fetched live.

query.description: Words of the SKU name or id, e.g. 'h100', 'openai gpt-5', 'official anthropic'. Empty matches every active SKU, first-party first.
query.title: Query

provider.description: Provider slug, e.g. vultr, ovhcloud, openai
provider.title: Provider

listing.description: Listing filter. current (default) = on the provider's public price page or product API; catalog_only = only in an order catalog, not on the public page; vanished = was listed, now missing; unknown = no public page to check against; all = everything. Every row carries listing_status.
listing.title: Listing

commitment.description: gpu and vps rows only. Default on-demand: standing list prices with no term and no interruption. spot, reserved, commit, dynamic or community select those rows; any shows every commitment.
commitment.title: Commitment

verbose.description: true = every field of every row (spec, all price points, extra, cite) and the coverage gaps
verbose.title: Verbose

tools.name: get_price
tools.description: Current list price of one SKU (id like vps/ovhcloud/vps-2027-model2 or llm/official/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5) with all secondary prices, USD/EUR equivalents, spec, source URL, verified_at, a stale flag that is true when the source's latest fetch failed (the price shown is then the last verified one), other listings of the same model, and headline_commit where the provider headlines a commitment price (a labelled secondary price; the primary price has no commitment). Returns an error object for an unknown id.

sku_id.description: SKU id as returned by search_skus, e.g. vps/ovhcloud/vps-2027-model2
sku_id.title: Sku Id

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: Price change points of a SKU over the last N days (default 90; a window of 14 days without a key, 30 with a free key, all of it with a paid key; the answer says which window applied): each row is when a price started to hold, with USD/EUR and the FX rate used. Rows are change points, not daily samples. Returns an error object for an unknown id.

sku_id.description: SKU id as returned by search_skus
sku_id.title: Sku Id

days.description: Look-back window in days, 1 to 30 with a free key, 14 without a key (a paid key reads all of it)
days.title: Days

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: Dated price changes, new SKUs, delistings and spec changes, newest first. Each row says when the change was first seen and the previous good snapshot it is measured against, plus the source id. Filter by since (ISO date), kind, category and provider.

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: Everything recorded since a date, for a model whose knowledge ends at a cutoff: price changes, new items, removals and retirements, newest first, each with its UTC date, the previous good snapshot, the source URL and a permanent link to the item. counts are for the whole period (not just the page); gaps names the sources that are stopped now, with the day they stopped (never filled in; outages that recovered are not recorded); record_begins says how far back the record goes. summary=true returns the largest percent moves per category (at most 40 entries) in one answer, ordered by size of the move, not by price. Paging: pass next_cursor back as cursor. Entries carry recorded values only, never a current price. Returns an error object for a bad date or filter. Same data as GET /v1/changes-since. Use this one to page through every entry or to filter by category and kind (price_change, new_item, removed_or_stopped, retirement); for a first look at what changed since your cutoff, with counts, scope llm/gpu/vps and the gaps, call what_changed_since instead.

since.description: UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. the day your knowledge ends
since.title: Since

category.description: vps, gpu, llm, inference or media
category.title: Category

summary.description: true = the largest moves per category in one answer
summary.title: Summary

tools.name: what_changed_since
tools.description: Call this when a user asks about current prices, models or retirements and your knowledge may be out of date: give the date your knowledge ends (YYYY-MM-DD, any date, no key needed) and get a short answer: a one-line summary, the counts of the whole period, and per group the entries a provider's own page or API shows: new models and plans, price changes (old to new, percent, date, source URL), retirements a provider's own lifecycle page dates (effective, and scheduled ones still ahead), and removed plans. kind=llm (LLM API models and inference hosts), gpu, vps or all. The default detail=brief lists first-party entries only (community catalogues such as models.dev and OpenRouter are counted, not listed), at most `limit` per group; detail=full returns every source class and every field (the history window of your key applies; without a key that is the most recent days). Entries carry recorded values only, never a current price: use search_skus or get_price for today's price. Returns an error object for a bad or future date. Retirements come from Azure VM and AWS Bedrock lifecycle pages only (other providers are not parsed). Same data as GET /v1/since and the page /prices/since/<date>. To page through every entry or filter by category use changes_since. Robots.txt changes of AI crawlers are a separate dataset (tool crawlers_changes).

date.description: UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD: the day your knowledge ends, e.g. 2026-06-01
date.title: Date

kind.description: all (default), llm (LLM API models and inference hosts), gpu or vps
kind.title: Kind

limit.description: Entries per group: 1 to 25 for brief (default 10), 1 to 200 for full (default 25)
limit.title: Limit

detail.description: brief (default): a few KB, first-party entries, any date. full: every entry and field, within your history window
detail.title: Detail

tools.name: black_friday_deals
tools.description: Black Friday 2026 VPS deals of providers we track, each with the stated price, the monthly price as stated for its term (a renewal price is never estimated), the lowest price we recorded for the same plan in the 30 days before the sealed moment (Fri 20 Nov 2026 11:00 UTC; fewer days where our history is shorter, see n_days and low_coverage), the difference between the two (difference_vs_lowest_30d, negative = below it) and links to the proof (archived observation, SKU history, sealed manifest). Facts only: where a comparison is not safe (other currency, VAT basis not stated, deal already in force, plan not in our history) it is null with its reason. `headline` counts, of the deals checked, how many were below the lowest price we recorded in the 30 days before the seal and how many were at or above it, with the as-of time. Each deal has a permanent page (links.permalink). Empty until providers publish deals.

max_eur_month.description: Maximum monthly price in EUR (USD deals converted at the stored ECB rate)
max_eur_month.title: Max Eur Month

eu_only.description: Only plans we know are deployable in the EU
eu_only.title: Eu Only

tools.name: check_deal
tools.description: Check one VPS deal: give an offer URL, or provider + plan + price. Returns the plan matched, the monthly price, the lowest price we recorded for that plan in the 30 days before the sealed moment, the difference, the VAT basis, the term, read dates and proof links. Refuses a price that is not one clear amount (regular and deal price together, intro-only, VAT words) and says why; returns candidates when the plan is ambiguous. A plan we do not track says so.

term.description: first_month | first_n_months | first_year | lifetime | recurring | unknown
term.title: Term

tools.name: get_uptime
tools.description: Uptime and latency of ~24 public AI API hosts (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Together, Fireworks, OpenRouter, Cohere, ElevenLabs, AWS Bedrock and more), measured by InfraRabbit itself every 5 minutes, not reported by the provider. Without `host`: every host with its current state and uptime %, p50 and p95 latency for the last 24 h, 7 d and 30 d. With `host` (the hostname, e.g. api.openai.com): its daily rows for `days` days and its incidents (two or more consecutive down windows, with start, end and evidence). Method: one unauthenticated HTTPS GET per host per round (DNS, TCP, TLS, time to first byte, HTTP status), from one vantage. It proves the provider's edge or gateway answered from there; it does NOT prove that a model generates or that your key, quota or region works. Check coverage_pct before quoting a figure: it says how much of the window was measured. Returns an error object for an unknown host. Same data as GET /v1/uptime and /v1/uptime/{host}/history and the pages /prices/uptime (status right now, worst first) and /prices/uptime/<provider>-api ("Is the OpenAI API down?").

host.description: Hostname as listed by this tool without a host, e.g. api.openai.com. Omit for every host.
host.title: Host

days.description: Days of daily rows and incidents when a host is given, 1 to 365
days.title: Days

tools.name: cheapest_for_spec
tools.description: Cheapest active SKUs meeting a minimum spec, ranked by list price only (no sponsorship, no affiliate weighting), excl. VAT (VAT-inclusive plans are ranked after removing their stated VAT rate). Starts with a short `answer` sentence (human names, price excl. VAT in the row's own currency, term, read date, source), then compact rows; each row carries price_excl_vat, source_class and, for GPUs, gpu_count and price_per_gpu_hour. Only first-party prices rank (the provider's own page or API); resellers, community catalogues (models.dev, LiteLLM, OpenRouter) and marketplaces take part only with include_community=true. gpu and vps default to commitment=on-demand: spot, reserved, committed, dynamic and community-cloud prices are left out unless commitment says otherwise. category vps|gpu|llm; vcpu, ram_gb, disk_gb minimums; gpu model substring (e.g. H100; with a memory size such as A100-80GB the card must state exactly that memory); region 'eu' for EU-deployable; currency USD|EUR for the ranking (rank.value is in that currency, rank.native_value in the row's own). verbose=true adds the full ranking method, every row field and the coverage gaps.

region.description: 'eu' for EU-deployable, 'us', 'asia', a country code such as nl or de (the places of the compare page), or a provider region code
region.title: Region

listing.description: Listing filter, default current: only plans on the provider's public price page or product API count. all includes catalog-only and vanished plans (each row carries listing_status).
listing.title: Listing

commitment.description: gpu and vps only. Default on-demand: standing list prices with no term and no interruption. spot, reserved, commit, dynamic or community select those rows; any shows every commitment (each row carries extra.commitment).
commitment.title: Commitment

include_stale.description: Also rank plans whose price is not verified (stale): after every current one, each flagged stale. Off by default.
include_stale.title: Include Stale

include_region_unstated.description: vps with a region filter only. A plan whose source states no region is never guessed into the place: it is left out of the rows, counted in region_unstated (count, and the cheapest of them). 1 = rank those plans with the others (the compare page's region_unknown=1).
include_region_unstated.title: Include Region Unstated

include_community.description: Also rank resellers (Amazon Bedrock, Azure ...), community catalogues (models.dev, LiteLLM, OpenRouter) and marketplaces; each row says source_class. Off by default: only the provider's own list prices rank.
include_community.title: Include Community

verbose.description: true = the full ranking method, every field of every row and the coverage gaps
verbose.title: Verbose

tools.name: vps_plans
tools.description: VPS plans as /prices/vps/plans and GET /v1/vps/plans return them: the very same function, so the answers cannot differ for the same filters. Every row is a plan with its verified list price a month (excl. VAT) for the chosen contract term, all price points the provider states, buying facts (IPv4, traffic, disk and vCPU type; null = not stated), region (region_stated=false when the source names none), verified_at and source_url. Only plans with a price verified in the last 3 days carry a price; the others are listed apart in not_verified without one. Sorted by price (or per GB RAM, per vCPU); nothing is ranked for money. Each plan has a detail_url with its facts sheet. Every plan carries price_excl_vat in the provider's own currency. Answers with a short `answer` first and compact plans; verbose=true returns everything. Answer pages for common searches: /prices/vps/cheapest.

max_price.description: Maximum price a month in the chosen currency
max_price.title: Max Price

region.description: A place key: eu, us, asia, a country code such as de or nl, or none (plans whose source states no region)
region.title: Region

term.description: Contract term: none = no commitment (default), 12 = up to 12 months, any
term.title: Term

ipv4.description: Only plans whose source states an own IPv4 address is included
ipv4.title: Ipv4

dedicated.description: Only plans whose source states dedicated vCPUs
dedicated.title: Dedicated

traffic_tb.description: Minimum included traffic in TB a month (unlimited counts)
traffic_tb.title: Traffic Tb

nvme.description: Only plans whose source states NVMe disks
nvme.title: Nvme

limit.description: Maximum plans returned, 1 to 500 (the same rows as the API; the API default is 200)
limit.title: Limit

verbose.description: true = every plan with all price points and facts, cheapest_per_provider, not_verified and the notes; default = a short answer and compact plans
verbose.title: Verbose

tools.name: stack_quote
tools.description: One call, the best current answer for a whole stack: a list of items (kind vps: vcpu, ram_gb, disk_gb, region, term, currency, count; kind gpu: gpu, count, hours_per_month, region, gpus_per_instance; kind llm or inference: model, input_mtok, output_mtok, count). Per item the 5 cheapest offers with a verified price (the free ordering: price only, nothing for money), the monthly cost for your count and usage (a stated unit price times your quantities, nothing estimated), verified_at, source_url and a scope line; an item with no fresh match says so. Totals per currency, never converted. Same answer as POST /v1/quote. Free: 3 quotes a day per address; beyond that 1 credit per quote on an API key (see /pricing). Reads prices, and records the free quote or credit it uses (so it is not read-only). Pass an idempotency_key to retry without a second charge. Returns an error object (HTTP 402 body) when out of credits.

idempotency_key.description: 1 to 128 characters; the same key never charges twice (API key callers)
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: Itemised cost of a usage profile at the SKU's current list price: tokens (input/output/cached) for LLM SKUs, hours/months for instances. Returns line items with the rates used, native, USD and EUR totals, verified_at and source_url. Pure arithmetic on stored prices; excl. VAT unless the result says otherwise.

sku_id.description: SKU id as returned by search_skus
sku_id.title: Sku Id

tools.name: get_index
tools.description: A named daily index series (e.g. eu-vps-floor-2c4g, h100-list-median, frontier-input-floor) with its latest value, the number of constituents and the constituents themselves, so the value can be recomputed. Omit series to list all series with their latest values. series=gpu-weekly is the weekly GPU price index: per GPU model (H100, H200, A100 80GB, L40S, RTX 4090, B200) the median and lowest first-party on-demand price per GPU-hour this week, last week and four weeks ago, with provider counts and method (page /prices/indices/gpu-weekly).

series.description: Series slug, or gpu-weekly for the weekly GPU price index; omit to list all series
series.title: Series

days.description: Look-back window in days, 1 to 3650; capped to your history window (14 days without a key, 30 with a free key, all of it with a paid key)
days.title: Days

tools.name: alert_me
tools.description: Where a person can get a free daily email when something changes: pass what to follow and get the subscribe URL to show them. kind = sku (a SKU id from search_skus: its price changes and retirement), provider (any change of a provider slug such as anthropic), category (vps, gpu, llm, inference or media), index (a series slug from get_index: moves of 5% or more) or new_model (new models of a provider). The person opens the URL, types their email address, confirms by link and gets at most one mail a day with a one-click unsubscribe. Nothing is sent from here and no address is taken by this tool. Returns an error object for an unknown target.

kind.description: What kind of thing to follow
kind.title: Kind

target.description: SKU id, provider slug, category, index series slug or provider slug (new_model)
target.title: Target
